thread.title: Why Is Apple Being Underappreciated? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Big Ticket Fund Managers
title: Why Is Apple Being Underappreciated? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Investment Thesis With Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) trading at a new 52-week high, some investors wonder if their reign is over, but I believe it has a long runway of continued growth. Apple bears under-appreciate the transition the company is making from merely a consumer technology provider to a software technology company. Growth in the company's service segment will be and currently is the next big driver for Apple. Investors have an opportunity now to invest in the future at the current cheap multiples.
The Apple Train Keeps Pushing Forward Despite The Naysayers Last month, Apple reported their Q2 earnings results that came in better than expected. Analysts piled on in the weeks leading up to the earnings release, cutting their estimates based on the earning results from some of Apple's top supplies. Bernstein, a notable AAPL analyst, cut their estimates , full year guidance, and price target for the year based on the results from the developers, and were dead wrong when Apple delivered their results. The new price target they presented was $170 for the next 12-months. As of today, Apple is trading above $193, well above their price target. We have seen this story before, analysts get too caught up with developers rather than the company itself.
Photo Credit
Apple reported revenue of $61.1 billion for the quarter compared to estimates of $60.8 billion, which was a 16% rise from Q2 2017. This was the fastest growth in more than two years. Earnings per share came in at $2.73 compared to estimates of $2.67. Here is a quick snapshot of the quarterly results.
Source: Chart created by author
As you can see, Q2 earnings brought a return of quality growth in almost every metric presented. Q2 outpaced growth in Q1 in all these areas, with the exception being gross margin. However, EPS and net income growth doubled from Q1 to Q2.
During the earnings release, Apple released Q3 revenue guidance of $51.5 billion to $53.5 billion, which also beat analysts' estimates of $51.61 billion. Overall, it seems like the majority of analysts got a little skittish prior to the release and were all dealt a "wake-up" call to not always listen to the rumors.
A Look At Segment Results Here is a quick look at the company's sales by product during Q2.
Source: Chart created by author
As you can see, iPhone sales continued to increase over prior year Q2, and grew at a slightly faster pace than Q1 as well. However, the true growth is found in the Services and Other Products, each growing 30.5% and 37.6%, respectively. This has been a continuing trend for these two areas over the course of the last couple of years.
Service revenue has grown 20+% over the past two years and does not look to be slowing down anytime soon considering the segment has grown 18% in Q1 and 31% in Q2, respectively. Service revenue includes the likes of Apple Music, the App Store, Apple Pay, and iCloud. Apple music reached a new high in Q2 with over 270 million paid subscribers now.
Other Products includes the likes of Apple TV, AirPods, and the Apple Watch. Much of the increase in this segment has been the success of the Apple Watch. Apple Watch once again saw its best quarter in Q2, a continued recent trend as of late, with a 50% growth in overall wearables. According to Apple Insider , the wearables business is now the size of a Fortune 300 company on its own.
Photo Credit
One of the areas that excite me the most about the company is its lessened reliance on the iPhone. Though the iPhone is still the main driver and continues to perform well, growth in other areas, particularly services revenue, has changed the sales mix. As you can see in the chart below, iPhone sales continue to be the main source of revenue, with over 60% of revenue related to its flagship product.
Source: Chart created by author
As I mentioned above, the growth in services revenue has been a major focus of the company moving forward as the segment has grown over 450 basis points, in terms of sales mix, since the end of 2015 and is now the second largest reportable segment for the company. Apple Music continues to be a solid growth driver for the company with revenues up 75% year over year during the quarter. The company is seeing their highest conversion rates yet, based on users who try the Apple Music system for free and convert to a paid subscription.
In terms of region, Americas continue to lead the charge with over 41% of total revenues coming from this region in Q2, followed by Europe and China, who account for 23% and 21%, respectively, of total revenues in Q2. An area for continued growth for the company is overseas, primarily China. China sales for the quarter were up 22% from prior year. Overseas areas, such as Japan, have been off to a great start in 2018, growing 26% and 22%, through the first two quarters, respectively.
Looking Ahead Innovation has always been the key to Apple's success since the release of the iPhone 1 back in 2007. Releasing innovative products with top of the line new technology has been what keeps Apple ticking. However, the question always arises from numerous bears on SA or elsewhere, can the company continue to innovate? Based on the track record, and the current products recently released, I would say the company is doing just fine. Also, as we have stated above, the company is taking advantage of their large iOS ecosystem, and transforming into more of a software company. The shift to more services is a much higher margin area for the company and is also a more predictable stream of revenues.
In addition to continually offering new and improved products, shifting to a higher margin and more reliable revenue stream through its services offerings, Apple also has a wealth of cash being repatriated along with new tax cuts enacted, which will all be utilized to continue increasing their dividend, buying back more stock, and make strategic acquisitions.
During the company's Q1 earnings call , CFO Luca Maestri responded to an analysts question around their plan for all their cash, stating that the company's goal is to be "cash neutral." Some of you may be asking yourself, well what do they mean by this? Great question! CEO Tim Cook clarified during the Q&A session that the company will have "an equal amount of cash and debt, and that they balance to zero." To give you an idea on how this looks, here is the company's cash vs debt balances over the past several years.
Source: The Motley Fool
As you can see in the chart above, the company's cash balance is growing at a much faster pace than their debt, which is great for investors. I would expect the company to continue to increase their dividend, which they recently did during their Q2 announcement, increasing the dividend 16%.
Valuation After a slow period for the stock between 2014 and 2016, the stock appears to be forming a new base that may be a solid entry point for those looking to ride the next wave up. Looking at the F.A.S.T. Graph chart below, the stock appears to be increasing at a faster rate than earnings over the last 8 years, but the business model is changing slightly and I believe a higher multiple is warranted.
Source: F.A.S.T. Graphs
Even with the slow period between the end of 2014 and 2016, AAPL stock has been on a tear over the last five years, gaining over 275% in value. The company has continued to launch new innovative products that have resonated well with the company's strong, cult like, customer base, which has continued to fuel higher growth around the globe. However, bearish investors still wonder whether the pipeline is reaching its tipping point. I feel as if we have heard this story from bears for years, but the company continues to prove them wrong. I have a hard time believing that a company that continues to grow and increase earnings at the pace Apple does, does not warrant a higher P/E. Look at how Apple stacks up to some of its tech peers over the past couple of years.
Source: The Motley Fool
Sure, they do not grow revenue as fast as Google ( GOOGL ) or Facebook ( FB ), but their EPS growth is second fastest to only FB. How does a stock like Microsoft ( MSFT ), which I also like, have a P/E above 80 and AAPL only warrants a multiple of 18? Obviously, there is more that goes into comparing a stock than its P/E multiple, but for simplicity purposes, it does not make a whole lot of sense at first glance.
When comparing other multiples, such a P/FCF and P/S, the stock appears overvalued when looking at their five-year history, however, the company continues to perform at a high level with hordes of cash at their disposal and a transformation into a dominant software company. Even at all-time highs for the stock, I feel the company is being underappreciated.
Conclusion As you know, AAPL is a cash cow, with nearly $267 billion in cash and marketable securities as of their latest quarterly filing . The company currently pays a dividend yielding 1.31% and has a payout ratio of only 24%. The combination of positive cash flows combined with a low payout ratio and tack changes, should continue to fund a growing dividend and provide investors with a strong buyback plan. The prospect of double digit dividend growth combined with aggressive stock appreciation bodes well for most investors.
Photo Credit
Based on the metrics above, the stock currently appears to be overvalued on paper; however, as we have eluded to above, we believe this blue-chip darling has a lot of room for growth as they continue to innovate, invest internationally, and transition to a dominant player in the software space. As an investor, one must analyze the true fundamentals of the company combined with their moat and potential growth moving forward to determine if the price today presents value for the future.
I hope everyone enjoyed the article and I look forward to hearing your viewpoints in the comments section below.
